title: design-language.md claims
description: One depth claim, as defined by docs/design/design-language.md. Every fenced jsonc block under a '### Claim:' heading in that document is validated against this schema by packages/content/test/unit/design-language-claims.test.ts. A claim is a falsifiable sentence, a decision procedure that would settle it, a pinned set of free parameters, a version, and a verdict. A claim with no procedure is not a claim; a verdict of not-measurable must say why.

claimId.description: Stable and permanent once any evidence file names it.

form.description: The claim verb. The vocabulary is closed: adding a form is a versioned amendment to design-language.md §3, not an edit to one claim.

subjects.description: What the claim is about, in the order the form's signature gives. Strategy ids, node ids, primitive ids, action ids as decimal strings, or the reserved token 'v1-strategy-pool'.

hypothesis.description: A sentence that could turn out to be false. Same standard as StrategyDefinition.hypothesis: 'plays broadly' is a description, 'whether breadth outruns the loss channel' is a hypothesis.

pinnedConstants.description: Every free parameter this claim invented. A constant that is not here is a constant nobody is guarding. Changing one without bumping definitionVersion is the failure this field exists to make visible.

definitionVersion.description: Bumped whenever the procedure or the pinned constants change. A verdict compared across a version bump is comparing two claims.

verdict.description: holds and refuted are readings. unmeasured means nobody has run it. not-measurable means the instrument does not exist, which is an honest answer and a different finding from a failure — the same distinction the metrics registry draws with its unavailable status.

verdictReason.description: Required when the verdict is not-measurable: what instrument is missing. Optional otherwise, for a one-line reading of the numbers.

evidence.description: Committed artefacts a reader can open. Required when the verdict is holds or refuted. Repository-relative paths, optionally with a heading anchor.

supersedes.description: Claim ids this one replaces. A refuted claim is not deleted; it is superseded, so the history of what was believed stays readable.

procedure.description: How the claim would be settled. Every field here is part of the claim's identity, which is why changing any of them bumps definitionVersion.

design.description: content-static needs no simulation and can be a unit test. Everything else needs a sweep, and the distinction is load-bearing: only the first can be enforced by npm run verify.

statistic.description: The quantity compared, named so two runs of this procedure compare the same thing.

measures.description: Metric ids from the balance metric registry, or reference-sweep measure ids. Required for every design except content-static.

runsPerArm.description: n per arm. Round-robin assignment is strategies[replicateIndex % poolSize], so a count that does not divide the pool measures a subset.

margin.description: The threshold the statistic must clear, written with its units. A claim may not name a threshold it did not pin, so this string is also expected to appear as a pinned constant.

interval.description: The uncertainty convention, e.g. wilson-95 or three-standard-errors. Absent means the claim is deterministic.

nullModel.description: Required for held-set designs. Set-geometry statistics are inflated by marginal totals alone — a nested-looking matrix arises by chance from row and column sums — so a held-set claim without a null model reports arithmetic as structure. See depth-and-skill.md §3.2.

refutedBy.description: The reading that would overturn the claim, stated before it is run. A claim that cannot say this is not falsifiable and does not belong in the language.
